candidates.speaker: Michael Ruse
candidates.proposition: Shared wonder at existence, natural regularities, consciousness, morality, and freedom does not uniquely support theism because the same experiences admit radically different interpretations.
candidates.attributionBasis: The direct address to Keith and the concluding description of their two contrasting paradigms identify Michael Ruse as the speaker.
candidates.loadBearingReason: This concluding synthesis directly addresses whether the phenomena under debate make best sense within theism or remain compatible with an agnostic naturalistic interpretation.

responseIntent.earlierTargetDescription: Keith Ward's appeal to the unexplained existence of natural regularities and related mysteries as congenial to a God-centered account.

candidates.contextSummary: After Ward expresses amazement at regularities in nature, Ruse agrees that existence and laws are mysterious but argues that they interpret the same experiences through fundamentally different paradigms.
